title: Micro‑clock ledger for token charge and cache adjustment telemetry
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We currently report request-level latency and token counts but cannot reliably attribute latency/cost to individual subtokens or account for KV/prefix cache effects. This prevents: (a) accurate per-token cost chargebacks, (b) root-causing quality regressions tied to cache misses, and (c) building token-level latency SLOs and rollups for the Console.

Goal: Implement a low-overhead micro-timing "ledger" emitted by the runtime that records per-subtoken timing slices (compute, cache-check, kv-apply) and cache-hit markers. Ingest these into our metrics/log pipeline and expose dashboards and traces that show per-request token timelines, cumulative token cost, and the delta when cache hits occur.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline from runtime -> event bus -> metrics store -> dashboards and trace explorer.
- Average added CPU overhead < 2% p50 and < 5% p95 on representative workloads.
- Telemetry volume bounded; estimates below 12% additional egress at 100k rps with current sampling strategy.
- Console dashboard showing per-request token latency waterfall and aggregate histograms by model/route.
- Billing reconciliation job demonstrates per-token cost attribution within 2% of baseline accounting for cache credits.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits per-subtoken microtimings with fields: request_id, model, route, token_index, delta_ns, phase (compute|kv|cache_check), cache_hit(boolean)
Events are consumed by the ingestion pipeline and materialized into a token_timings topic and a summarized metrics stream
Dashboard panel in Console per-route displaying token waterfall and token-level p50/p95 latencies
End-to-end performance overhead and telemetry volume validated against benchmark harness (results attached)
implementation_notes: Runtime: add a lightweight per-request ring buffer (preallocated for typical max tokens) that records micro-slices as pairs of (phase, delta_ns) and a cache_hit flag for 'cache_check' phase.
Serialization: protobuffers v3 with field ids reused across releases to keep payload small. Use delta-encoding for token_index and timestamps to reduce size.
Sampling: default adaptive sampling at 1% but increase to 5% for requests that hit error-rate thresholds or belong to flagged customers (configurable in Console)
Ingestion: token_timings topic -> stream processor to produce summarized metrics (per-route token histograms) and per-request timeline events for trace explorer
Privacy: strip user prompt text from telemetry; only metadata kept. Customer opt-out path respected (no telemetry emitted for customers with off flag)
Backward compatibility: ensure new runtime field optional and tolerant if downstream consumers not updated. Provide a shim in router that can synthesize coarse events for older runtimes.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Full-fidelity telemetry for every token produces high egress and storage costs. Chosen approach: adaptive sampling + delta summaries to limit cost while keeping signal for debugging and billing.
Timing resolution vs overhead: 1us resolution provides good signal but increases integer size. We selected ns deltas with varint encoding; benchmarked overhead acceptable on tested GPUs/CPUs.

Caching attribution ambiguity: cross-request shared cache warmups can make attribution noisy. We will report 'cache_credit' as aggregate deltas over sliding windows to ameliorate noise for billing reconciliation.

Complexity in ingestion: requires stream processor changes and index strategies. Risk: delayed dashboard availability if materialization fails; mitigations include fallbacks to sampled logs and an alerting runbook.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement runtime ring buffer + basic emitter behind feature flag (internal-only). Build unit tests and microbench harness.
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 1% sampled traffic in staging and then in canary region for 2 weeks. Validate CPU overhead and egress numbers. Review metrics and dashboards.
Phase 3 (gradual): raise sampling for flagged customers and expand to 5% global if telemetry budgets permit. Turn on ingestion summarization jobs.
Phase 4 (GA): expose Console views and billing reconciliation summaries; document SLOs and add automation to trigger higher sampling on regressions.
test_plan: Microbench harness that generates synthetic prompts at variable seq lengths and measures overhead with/without ledger enabled
Integration test that validates events reach token_timings topic and summarized metrics match expected distributions
End-to-end smoke that renders Console waterfall for sampled requests and validates fields present
Load test at 100k rps sample rate to verify ingestion and storage limits
